**Reasoning as myself:**

I have been farming this same land in Quzhou for over forty years. My husband is gone now, and my son lives in Beijing. I manage about 5 mu myself, with hired help at planting and harvest time — I cannot do the heavy work anymore at my age.

I will grow what I always grow: winter wheat and summer corn on the same 5 mu. This rotation is what I know. The seed shop in the village sells Kenong 199 wheat seed and hybrid corn seed, same as my neighbors use. I would not know how to manage something different, and there is no one to help me figure it out.

For wheat I put in rotary tillage in October before seeding, then water it four times through the season — once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading, and once during grain filling. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and top up with urea in spring. I spray herbicide in early spring and one more time for insects and rust near heading. I expect about 450 jin per mu if the weather is decent.

For corn I hire a machine to plant right after the wheat comes off in June. The summer rains help, but I usually water twice if it is dry. I apply fertilizer twice — some at planting, some when the plants are knee-high. One herbicide spray early, one for the corn borer later. I harvest in late September. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

I do not experiment. At 67, a bad season means real hardship. I stay with what I know works.
